p1.title: CSRF enforced-by-default in prod (warn-mode opt-out only)
p1.evidence: apps/api/src/security/csrf.middleware.ts:177-179 enforce = !(CSRF_ENFORCE==='false' || CSRF_WARN==='true') — i.e. missing env = ENFORCED; :243-248 throws ForbiddenException on invalid token. Bearer-token requests are exempted (213-215) which is correct (CSRF threat model is ambient creds). Action is config-only: ensure CSRF_ENFORCE/CSRF_WARN are unset on Railway.
p1.fixSketch: ACTION (Greg): verify neither CSRF_ENFORCE=false nor CSRF_WARN=true is set on Railway prod. Default (unset) = enforced; no code change.

verdict.reason: Independently re-read apps/api/src/security/csrf.middleware.ts. Lines 177-179: enforce = !(process.env.CSRF_ENFORCE === 'false' || process.env.CSRF_WARN === 'true') — with both env vars unset the inner OR is false, so enforce = !false = true. CSRF is ENFORCED by default, confirming the claim. Lines 243-249: when enforce is true, throws ForbiddenException({error:'CsrfError', message:'Invalid or missing CSRF token'}) on an invalid/missing token (token validity computed at 217-227 via constant-time safeEquals of cookie vs x-csrf-token header). Bearer-token exemption (213-215, /^Bearer\s+\S+/i) is correct — CSRF's threat model is ambient credentials, and a Bearer header is never auto-attached cross-site; this is the Vercel→Railway cross-origin path so most authed mutations ride Bearer. Comment block 170-176 documents this as sec-fix wave1 #7 (default flipped from warn to enforce so a forgotten env can't silently disable protection). Code is in the secure state; the only residual is the config assertion (no CSRF_ENFORCE=false / CSRF_WARN=true on Railway prod), which I cannot verify from read-only code — so the item legitimately remains as a config-verify task. P1 and no-config are correct; not P0 because the secure default is the code default, not a code hole.
verdict.refinedFix: No code change. Pre-launch config check (Greg): in Railway prod env, confirm CSRF_ENFORCE is not set to "false" and CSRF_WARN is not set to "true" (either unset, or CSRF_ENFORCE set to anything other than the literal "false"). Default (both unset) = enforced. Optionally add a boot-time log line echoing the resolved enforce mode so the active state is visible in Railway deploy logs.

p1.title: EMAIL_FROM defaults to onboarding@resend.dev sandbox — password-reset/invite/welcome mail will be silently dropped for all non-owner recipients
p1.evidence: apps/api/src/email/email.service.ts:412 const from = process.env.EMAIL_FROM || 'VenueOS <onboarding@resend.dev>'. p1.fixSketch: ACTION (Greg): (1) verify a sending domain in the Resend dashboard; (2) set RESEND_API_KEY + EMAIL_FROM='VenueOS <noreply@yourdomain>' on Railway. verdict.reason: Re-read email.service.ts:412 — `const from = process.env.EMAIL_FROM || 'VenueOS <onboarding@resend.dev>'` is exactly as cited; this default is the Resend sandbox sender, which only delivers to the Resend account owner. isConfigured() (379-380) gates solely on RESEND_API_KEY, and #dispatch (397-404) throws honestly in prod ONLY when the key is unset — so the "lying check-your-inbox" case is handled, but the SET-key + default-FROM case is NOT: it builds a real payload (418-424) and POSTs to Resend (426), which silently drops every non-owner recipient. Confirmed the two impacted prod flows: welcome mail fires for every public self-signup at onboarding.service.ts:180 (sendWelcome to user.email), and password-reset depends on the same dispatcher. So with a key set but EMAIL_FROM left default, no operator/admin/parent (anyone but the account owner) receives welcome or reset mail. Code path is correct; the fix is a Railway/Resend deploy-config action, hence no-config. P1 not P0: it doesn't crash a core flow or break a sold feature's code, but it silently breaks all non-owner transactional mail — a real launch gap. CLAUDE.md's EMAIL_FROM entry independently documents this as the usual root cause of "no emails arrive."
verdict.refinedFix: ACTION (Greg, deploy-config — no code change): (1) In the Resend dashboard, verify a real sending domain (add the DKIM/SPF/DMARC DNS records). (2) On Railway, set both RESEND_API_KEY and EMAIL_FROM='VenueOS <noreply@yourverifieddomain>' (and optionally EMAIL_REPLY_TO), then redeploy. Optional code hardening (separate, lower priority): on prod boot, warn/refuse if EMAIL_FROM is unset or still equals the onboarding@resend.dev default while RESEND_API_KEY is set, to make this trap loud instead of silent.

p1.fixSketch: Create/move floor-plan objects to a PRIVATE Supabase bucket and serve via short-TTL signed URLs (the floor-plans controller already has signed-URL plumbing — floor-plans.controller.ts:215-220). verdict.reason: Independently re-read all cited code. supabase-storage.service.ts:81 and :96 set the single 'assets' bucket public:true on create AND update. floor-plans.controller.ts:467,470 upload floor plans into that same public bucket at `${tenantId}/floor-plans/...` (BUCKET='assets' at storage:4), and the controller's own comment at :464 admits the bucket is public. So the permanent public URL (`/object/public/assets/{tenantId}/floor-plans/...`) resolves for anyone who has it — tenant path is obscurity, not access control. Confirmed real and current on master; task #200 tracks the full fix as still pending. NUANCE the finding omitted: a PARTIAL mitigation already exists — withSignedImageUrl (controller:238-243, 15-min TTL at :218) re-signs the imageUrl on EVERY read path (list :282, get :347, create :533), so the API never emits the permanent public URL. That reduces but does not close the exposure (leaked-URL/cache/referrer still resolves against the public bucket; the :215-218 comment says exactly this). Severity P1 (not P0): not directly enumerable (random suffix+timestamp), and the permanent URL is no longer surfaced by the API, so practical exploitation needs an already-leaked URL. Fix sketch is sound: move to a private bucket served via the already-wired createSignedUrl plumbing; only the bucket-split-vs-RLS choice is a decision, the rest is mechanical.
verdict.refinedFix: Create a separate PRIVATE Supabase bucket (e.g. 'floor-plans') with public:false, and route floor-plan uploads there instead of the public 'assets' bucket (change BUCKET target only for the floor-plans upload path). Serving is already done correctly via withSignedImageUrl + createSignedUrl, so reads keep working with no controller changes beyond the bucket name. This keeps signage assets CDN-cacheable in the public bucket while floor plans require a signed read. One-time migration: copy existing `${tenantId}/floor-plans/*` objects from 'assets' to the new private bucket and update FloorPlan.imageUrl rows (pathFromObjectUrl at storage:253 already derives the path). Decision needed: dedicated private bucket (recommended, simplest given existing signed plumbing) vs RLS on the shared bucket.

So 'AI board -> on a screen' is generate (phone OK) -> move to desktop to arrange -> build playlist -> publish: multi-step + blocked on phone, confirming the claim. NOT P0: the flow is completable end-to-end and nothing is broken/costume — it's friction + a desktop dependency on the most-marketed flow, so P1 stands. codeFixable=yes (new UI action). This collapses generate->arrange->playlist->publish (4 steps + a desktop) into generate->put-on-screen (2 taps, phone-only). Keep 'Use this'/Edit as the desktop arrange path; the new button is the express lane. Verify on a <=1023px viewport that the new action does not route through openInBuilder.
